newsitem.title: FRANCE: Legras sees EU grain use higher than expected.
newsitem.headline: Legras sees EU grain use higher than expected.

text.p: The European Commission's chief permanent agriculture official, Guy Legras, predicted on Monday that EU grain consumption would be higher than forecast this season, limiting the amount of grain ending up in intervention.
"There is a very strong increase in (EU) consumption. All the figures...show that there is a stronger increase than expected," he told Reuters by telephone from Brussels.
Legras, director general for agriculture at the European Commission, declined to give a figure but said his forecast was based on trends in both animal and human consumption of grain.
"For this reason there will not be a lot of grain going into intervention," he said.
Last month, grain market sources estimated total cereals consumption in the 15-nation EU at 171.20 million tonnes for 1996/97 (July/June).
Of this, 107.2 million tonnes would be in the animal feed sector, they said.

Estimates compiled around the same time by the Commission from data supplied by member states pegged total consumption at 167 million tonnes. From that total some 102.5 million tonnes would be going into animal feed, the estimates showed.
Legras did not say which figure he regarded as the current consensus forecast.
